ma_scotland_boulder_aka_haystack_boulder.blurb: A single large block in the woods on the southern edge of Newburyport, close to the interstate, and possibly the northernmost bouldering in the state. It holds 17 problems between V0 and V4, with most clustered at V2 through V4. The block stands up to roughly 20 feet, so a few lines are highball, and some of the stone is loose, so test holds before pulling. It makes a relaxed, social hangout spot for a short session rather than a full day, and the walk from the car is only a couple of hundred yards on trail.

ma_the_marsh_caves.blurb: A compact cluster of boulders in Douglas State Forest, reached by a short woodland hike beside a swamp. The draw is steep stone: a heavily overhanging block, a deep cave and a precarious detached block that is strictly climb-at-your-own-risk. Seventeen problems are recorded, mostly V0 to V4 with a core around V2 and V3, then a few serious hard lines from V6 up to V9 and several projects still open. Quality is generally high and the style leans powerful and steep. Sun exposure is not documented, and this is a spot for a focused session rather than a big circuit.

ma_lower_walls.blurb: A set of short east-facing conglomerate walls in the Hammond Pond area just west of Boston, often a climber's first outdoor day. Faces top out around 35 feet or less, so this is single-pitch climbing with a mix of top-rope setups, gear leads and a lone hard boulder problem. Of the 16 climbs, most are easy to moderate, ranging from scrambly ground up to roughly 5.8. Bring long slings for anchors, and watch for slippery leaves at the lip. Crowds are mostly locals, as the area is not considered a destination.

ma_mormon_hollow_left_side.blurb: The left half of Mormon Hollow, a gneiss cliff in Wendell in western Massachusetts. It is split into four sections: a far-left wall of solid 5.10s and 5.11s, a big roof cave with a short run of hard sport lines in the 5.12 to 5.13 range, a small area with trad and sport odds and ends, and a buttress with an area classic arete and a steep, bouldery 5.12 test piece. Of 16 climbs, most are sport, with a few trad lines, a top-rope and one boulder problem. Expect overhangs, roofs and powerful moves; easier options exist but are few.
ma_mormon_hollow_left_side.parking_note: Pull off roadside at the T-junction where Davis Road meets Coldbrook Road, leaving the field entrances on both sides clear.

ma_02_main_face.blurb: The tallest and busiest section of Rose Ledge, a short gneiss cliff line in Northfield with horizontal cracks and features. Cliffs here run to about 50 feet, so everything is quick single-pitch work. Sixteen climbs mix trad leads and top-ropes, with a broad spread: a handful of easy routes, a solid middle band around 5.8 to 5.10, and a few hard lines reaching the low 5.12 range. Most people top-rope, though many routes take gear well, which makes this a good place for moderates and for newer leaders building experience. Expect company on nice weekends.

ma_weetamoo_boulder.blurb: One of the named boulders in the Weetamoo area of Lynn Woods, an area known for the densest collection of quality problems in the park. The block carries 16 problems, all bouldering, with a middle cluster of V3 and V4 and a notable group of V7 lines, plus a few harder ones into V9. Some problems are slopey arete lines; others are crack problems. It is a walk of about half an hour from the main lot along a wide dirt road and then a faint climbers' trail, past neighboring boulders on the way. Mountain bikers share the paths.

ma_cloud_buttress.blurb: The first cliff you meet at Hanging Mountain in Sandisfield, in southwestern Massachusetts, a short walk up the trail from the lot. A compact buttress with 16 routes split evenly between sport and trad, plus some mixed-protection lines. The grades skew hard: one or two moderates near 5.7 to 5.10, then a thick band of 5.11 and 5.12 and a single 5.13. Steep, sustained climbing is the theme, with a standout crack as the trad highlight. The wider cliff faces southeast and the rock can be loose in places, so wear a helmet and be careful when belaying.
